notes: New in 2.3.8: your assistant can now use websites for you. 1) It has its own browser: it opens websites, clicks buttons, fills in forms and reads the page, like a person would. Just ask, for example "sign up for a free picture-making service and set it up". This needs the browser on your server. If you haven't yet, run this one time: sudo bash /opt/myassistant/current/optional/install-browser.sh 2) Sign-ups: it always asks you first, like "Sign up at example.com with you@gmail.com?". Reply YES and it continues. It uses your connected Gmail, reads the code or link the site sends there by itself, and makes a strong password. The password is saved encrypted on your server. You can see it in Settings → Browser & logins → Saved logins (tap Show; only works while you are logged in). It is never in the chat or the Activity log. If you wanted a key (an "API key"), it makes the key on the site and, after your YES, saves it straight into Settings → Brain → AI keys (or the Vault). It never shows the key in the chat. 3) Robot checks: if a site shows "I'm not a robot", it sends you a link. Open it on your phone (log in if asked): you see its browser live. Tap where you would tap on the site, type if needed, then tap Done (or reply "done"). It then carries on. 4) It never pays, never types card details, never picks a paid plan and never gives a phone number. If a site wants that, it stops and tells you. You can switch all of this off in Settings → Browser & logins → Browser actions. Logins and cookies are kept between uses; the browser closes itself after 10 minutes without use.
